chill.title: Fløibanen at Dusk, Walk Down
chill.description: The funicular to the Fløyen summit has run since 1918 — take it up at golden hour, walk the summit forest trails, then hike the 4 km path down through birch woods as the fjord city lights up below you.
chill.bonus: Leave your phone in your pocket from the summit to the bottom. Full blackout descent.

chill.title: Afternoon at KODE Art Museums
chill.description: Norway's largest art museum complex spreads across four buildings on the lakeside — the Edvard Munch collection in KODE 3 rivals Oslo's, and the design collection in KODE 2 rewards the kind of slow looking that galleries rarely get.
chill.bonus: Find one piece that genuinely unsettles you. Stay in front of it long enough to figure out why.

chill.title: Golden Hour Walk on Bryggen Wharf
chill.description: The 14th-century Hanseatic wooden wharf is Bergen's most photographed place for a reason — but it's the narrow alleys behind the painted facades, full of bookshops and silversmiths, that no postcard captures.
chill.bonus: Find the most interesting shop in the back alleys. Buy something small from it.

chill.title: Slow Morning in the Nøstet Quarter
chill.description: Bergen's old fishermen's quarter is the city's most intact neighbourhood — painted wooden houses on a harbour promenade, a coffee shop every hundred metres, and zero tourists before 10am.
chill.bonus: Leave your phone in your pocket for the first hour. Walk without a destination.

adventure.title: Sea Kayak the Osterfjord
adventure.description: Paddle through one of Norway's deepest fjords on a guided half-day tour from Espeland — 30 minutes from Bergen. The water is arctic-clear and the cliffs on either side rise 300 metres straight up.
adventure.bonus: Swim at least once. The fjord is cold. That's the point.

adventure.title: Tandem Paraglide Over Voss
adventure.description: Voss Active launches tandem paragliding flights from the mountainside above town — you and a pilot clip in, run off a ridge, and spend 20 minutes suspended above a valley the Vikings named. Book at least a week ahead.
adventure.bonus: Don't look down until you're fully airborne. Earn the view.

adventure.title: Climb Ulriken at First Light
adventure.description: Bergen's tallest city mountain rises to 643 metres — the trail from the cable-car base cuts through birch forest to a summit with a 360-degree panorama over the seven mountains and the fjord below.
adventure.bonus: Summit without checking your phone once. Full blackout from trailhead to peak.

adventure.title: Via Ferrata at Voss
adventure.description: An hour by train from Bergen, Voss Active runs guided via ferrata routes on sheer rock faces above the valley — iron rungs and cables on near-vertical stone, no climbing experience required, full commitment needed.
adventure.bonus: Look straight down for a full ten seconds at the highest clip point. Don't step back first.

foodie.title: Tasting Menu at Lysverket
foodie.description: Christopher Haatuft's restaurant occupies the ground floor of the KODE museum — a New Nordic tasting menu built around what coastal Norway catches and grows, executed with the precision of a chef who left New York to cook this food specifically.
foodie.bonus: Ask your server what Haatuft is most proud of right now. Order whatever they say.

foodie.title: Lunch by Boat at Cornelius Seafood Restaurant
foodie.description: The only way to Cornelius is a 20-minute complimentary boat ride from Bryggen pier — the restaurant sits on its own island in the Korsfjord with no road access. The seafood is whatever the fjord provided that morning.
foodie.bonus: Take the slower return boat. Don't check the time.

foodie.title: Shrimp Cone at the Bergen Fish Market
foodie.description: Fisketorget has sold fresh shrimp in cones since the city has been a city — buy one, eat it on the quay at the edge of the Vågen harbour, and don't photograph it until the third bite.
foodie.bonus: Order in Norwegian. "En rekekjeks, takk." Commit regardless of how it goes.

social.title: Live Concert at Hulen
social.description: One of the oldest underground rock clubs in Norway — built into a WWII bomb shelter beneath the University in 1968. Check the schedule before you go; the energy is better when you don't know the act.
social.bonus: Talk to someone standing near you before the main act starts. Get their name.

social.title: Craft Beer at 7 Fjell Bryggeri Taproom
social.description: Bergen's most respected microbrewery runs a city-centre taproom where the rotation changes monthly — seasonal ales, sours, and a Bavarian-style pilsner that holds up against anything Munich brews.
social.bonus: Ask the bartender what they're most proud of brewing right now. Order that.

social.title: Nygårdsgate Bar Crawl
social.description: The strip of bars running from the student neighbourhood toward the waterfront is Bergen's most varied evening sequence — cocktail bars next to dive bars next to craft beer spots, all within a 600-metre walk.
social.bonus: Have at least one real conversation with a stranger at every stop. Not small talk — something real.

active.title: Swim at Nordnes Sjøbad
active.description: Bergen's historic outdoor saltwater pool on the tip of the Nordnes peninsula has been open since 1855 — 50-metre lanes, diving platforms, and cold North Sea water at the edge of the fjord.
active.bonus: Jump from the highest platform. No looking down first.

active.title: Bouldering at Klatresenteret Bergen
active.description: Bergen's best bouldering gym has 1,200 sqm of routes from V0 to V11 with overhangs designed by a competition route-setter. No partner or gear required — rent shoes, buy a day pass, stay until your forearms have an opinion about it.
active.bonus: Attempt a route one grade harder than you think you can complete. Try it at least five times.

active.title: The Sognefjord Day Trip
active.description: Bergen's best full-day excursion: train to Myrdal, Flåm Railway descent through waterfalls, express boat through the UNESCO Nærøyfjord, bus over the mountain, train back. Leave at 7am and return by 9pm with a complete rearrangement of your sense of scale.
active.bonus: No podcasts or music on the fjord boat. The Nærøyfjord's silence is the whole point.

active.title: Run the Syv Fjell Ridge Segment
active.description: Bergen is ringed by seven named mountains — the shortened Ulriken-to-Fløyen ridgeline run covers 15 km of trail with fjord views the entire route and one brutal descent that earns the beer waiting at the bottom.
active.bonus: No headphones. The mountains have their own soundtrack.
